clue.text: Judge and I am occupying large country residence

indicators.note: to occupy a house is to be inside it, so the words I am go within the residence

parts.note: an estate is a large country property with its house and land
I am contracts to I'm, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A judge, like an aristocrat, is described as living in a grand country house.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity is to estimate it, making a rough assessment or guess.

clue.text: Test moved to the afternoon?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a formal examination of knowledge
second meaning: read as two pieces, formerly (ex) morning (a.m.), as anything shifted past noon is

explanation.surface: A school test has been rescheduled from morning to afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two pieces: EX (former, no longer) and AM (ante meridiem, the morning). Something moved into the afternoon has stopped being AM.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge, as taken at school or university.

clue.text: Shot one pellet wildly? One's good with shots

indicators.note: letters going wildly are flung about at random, so the words shot one pellet are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fires a pellet off at random; the question is whether they are a good shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' and 'shots' both suggest guns, but the second means photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto lens lets a photographer take good long-distance pictures, so it is a thing that helps with photographic shots.

clue.text: Player notes one of the rugby backs

parts.note: musical notes together make music
a centre is one of the back-line positions in a rugby team

explanation.surface: A rugby player is noted down as one of the team's backs.
explanation.definitionFit: A music centre is a hi-fi unit that plays records, tapes and CDs, so it is a player of music.

clue.text: Cork, when top's blown, will do for stylish hat

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, so losing it means dropping the first letter of the cork

parts.note: a cork is a stopper for a bottle

explanation.surface: A cork that pops off a bottle is jokingly said to serve as a fancy hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cork' looks like the Irish city but is the bottle stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A topper is a top hat, the tall formal silk hat worn with morning dress.

clue.text: Class-conscious one's to be tearful, preserving name

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safely within, so the name abbreviation sits inside

parts.note: to sob is to weep, to be tearful

explanation.surface: A status-obsessed person weeps but keeps their good name intact.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob looks down on people of lower social standing, being very conscious of social class.

clue.text: I absolutely won't say this about another's autobiography?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an emphatic refusal, 'no way'
second meaning: read literally, a book about someone else's life is ...

explanation.walkthrough: The second half takes the phrase literally: an autobiography is a book on the writer's own life, so one by someone else is not on yours.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a forceful way of refusing, meaning certainly not, under no circumstances.

clue.text: Idiot — there's just one H in "spheroid"

indicators.note: one H placed in the spheroid means these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a bead is a small round ball, a spheroid
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pedant points out that spheroid is spelt with only a single H.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's just' is padding; the clue says to put ONE H in a bead, the small sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonehead is a slang word for a stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Finally cut down book of maps

indicators.note: a thing cut down is shortened, here by losing its final letter

parts.note: finally means at last

explanation.surface: A book of maps has at last been abridged.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, a reference book for geography.

clue.text: Moralistic type's play on words taking in girl

indicators.note: to take in is to contain or admit, so the girl's name goes inside the pun

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A prudish person's wordplay involves a girl, perhaps a risqué joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A Puritan is someone with strict moral or religious principles who disapproves of pleasure.

clue.text: A guide to Tom's domination?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rough practical principle
second meaning: rule by Tom Thumb, the tiny folk-tale hero

explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized boy of the English fairy tale, so his rule would be the rule of Thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule of thumb is an approximate method based on experience, a practical guideline.

clue.text: Meal at work? Spooner's had no impact

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the first letters of the two words trade places

parts.note: to have no is to lack, so had no means lacked
punch means impact or forcefulness

explanation.surface: Someone's lunch at the office was underwhelming.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening letters of LACKED PUNCH gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed lunch is food prepared at home and carried to eat at school or the office.

clue.text: Something to see with Bond, say, taking drink

parts.note: James Bond is an example of a spy
a glass is a drink, as in a glass of wine

explanation.surface: James Bond sees things clearly while having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small hand-held telescope used for viewing distant objects.

clue.text: Support the Spanish drive

parts.note: a prop is a support
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Backing a Spanish driving project or player.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel is to push forward or move along, a synonym of the verb drive.

clue.text: Expression of surprise on encountering a feature of eclipse

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gasps on seeing a solar eclipse.
explanation.definitionFit: The corona is the sun's halo-like outer atmosphere, visible during a total solar eclipse.

clue.text: Firm supporting a lot of recent painting

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporter is underneath, so the firm comes after
most but not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: fresh means new or recent
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company backs most of the recent paintings, as an arts sponsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a wall painting done on wet plaster, a kind of mural.

clue.text: One producing spirited autobiography?

parts.note: spirited is taken as written by a spirit, a phantom; such a person writes celebrities' autobiographies for them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' looks like lively, but here it means written by a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter writes books, often memoirs, that are published under another person's name.

clue.text: Misprint in dirty poem

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of letters across the words dirty poem

explanation.surface: An error has crept into a smutty verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typographical error, a mistake in printed or typed text.

clue.text: Polluted seas filled with sticky stuff for all time

indicators.note: the sticky stuff fills the gap, going inside the mixed-up letters
polluted water is fouled and disturbed, so the letters of seas are mixed up

parts.note: gel is a sticky jelly-like substance

explanation.surface: Seas fouled with oily sludge stay contaminated forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polluted' and 'sticky stuff' paint an oil spill, but 'Polluted' only tells you to rearrange the word seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageless means eternal, never growing old, so it lasts for all time.

clue.text: One demanding freedom from retribution, dismissing naughty child

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so the naughty child's letters are removed

parts.note: impunity is exemption from punishment
an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: Someone calls for an amnesty but sends away a badly behaved child.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity is the state of being one, a single whole; it is also the number one in mathematics.

clue.text: Call for assistance initially over working indifferently

indicators.note: the distress call comes at the start, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over, a set of six balls

explanation.surface: An emergency call is made first after someone has been working half-heartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means only moderately well, neither good nor bad, which is how something done indifferently turns out.

clue.text: A few run out clutching British headwear

indicators.note: to clutch is to grip, holding the British abbreviation inside

parts.note: some means a few
RO is the cricket abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: Some batsmen are dismissed while gripping a British hat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is run out when the stumps are broken before they reach the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a wide-brimmed Mexican hat, an item of headwear.
